high.title: Government Offers Tax Incentives at Indonesia International Financial Center (PFII) — Here Are the Details
high.summary: The newly enacted PFII Law grants sweeping tax incentives including income tax, VAT, and customs exemptions to businesses operating within Indonesia's International Financial Center, with income tax relief valid for up to 50 years for qualifying foreign tax subjects. The incentives cover 18 categories of financial and investment service activities, making PFII a highly attractive destination for foreign capital. This is a landmark regulatory development that could significantly reshape Indonesia's financial landscape and attract major international financial institutions.

high.title: PFII's Initial Capital: Not Relying on State Budget — Where Does the Funding Come From?
high.summary: The newly passed PFII Law stipulates that the initial capital for the PFII Management Institution will come primarily from Danantara (BPI Daya Anagata Nusantara), Indonesia's sovereign investment body, classified as a special investment. Additional funding sources include private businesses, donated state/regional assets, and other legally permitted funding channels. This confirms Danantara's central role in financing major national strategic projects and signals significant capital deployment from Indonesia's sovereign wealth fund.

high.title: Foreign Capital of Rp 1.3 Trillion Exits Indonesian Capital Market
high.summary: Foreign investors recorded a net sell of Rp 1.36 trillion on Friday (24/7) as the Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) weakened due to global uncertainty from new US tariffs and Middle East conflict. Cumulative net foreign selling throughout 2026 has nearly reached Rp 80 trillion, with year-to-date net foreign sell standing at Rp 79.09 trillion. This sustained capital outflow signals significant pressure on Indonesian equities and warrants close monitoring by investors.

high.title: Asian Stock Markets Fall, IHSG Plunges Nearly 2%
high.summary: The Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) dropped sharply by 1.75% to 6,204.63 in the first trading session on Friday (24/7), briefly falling more than 2% to 6,161.13, in line with broader declines across global markets. Trading volume reached 24.60 billion shares with a transaction value of Rp 10.51 trillion. The sharp decline reflects heightened global risk-off sentiment and poses significant implications for Indonesian equity investors.

high.title: Watch Out: Tax Amnesty Participants Who Have Not Repatriated Assets Will Be Audited
high.summary: Finance Minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa announced stricter enforcement against Tax Amnesty and Voluntary Disclosure Program (PPS) participants who have not yet repatriated their overseas assets to Indonesia. The Ministry of Finance will conduct tax audits on all incoming funds, in collaboration with the Financial Transaction Reports and Analysis Center (PPATK), targeting non-compliant taxpayers. This policy shift signals a more aggressive tax enforcement stance that could impact high-net-worth individuals and businesses with offshore assets.

high.title: Perry Warjiyo Resigns as Bank Indonesia Governor
high.summary: Bank Indonesia Governor Perry Warjiyo has officially resigned, with President Prabowo Subianto receiving his resignation letter on July 26, 2026. Senior Deputy Governor Destry Damayanti has been appointed as Acting Governor in the interim. This is a major market-moving event as central bank leadership changes can significantly impact monetary policy direction, rupiah stability, and investor confidence.

high.title: Destry Damayanti Appointed as Acting Bank Indonesia Governor
high.summary: Senior Deputy Governor Destry Damayanti has been officially appointed as Acting Governor of Bank Indonesia following Perry Warjiyo's resignation, as mandated by Indonesian banking law. The transition is being handled in accordance with the Bank Indonesia Act, ensuring institutional continuity. Markets will closely watch for any signals regarding monetary policy continuity during this leadership transition period.

high.title: Perry Warjiyo's Reason for Resigning as Bank Indonesia Governor
high.summary: Perry Warjiyo voluntarily resigned as Bank Indonesia Governor on July 25, 2026, citing personal reasons, with Destry Damayanti confirmed as interim Acting Governor. The voluntary and personal nature of the resignation provides some reassurance against speculation of policy-driven departures. Investors will be monitoring the stability of monetary policy and rupiah management under the new interim leadership.

high.title: Process for Selecting New Bank Indonesia Governor Following Perry Warjiyo's Resignation
high.summary: Following Perry Warjiyo's resignation, the process for selecting a new Bank Indonesia Governor is governed by Law No. 4 of 2026 on the Amendment to the Financial Sector Development and Strengthening (P2SK) Law, requiring President Prabowo to appoint a new governor. The formal selection process introduces a period of leadership uncertainty at Indonesia's central bank, which is critical for monetary policy, interest rate decisions, and currency management. Investors should monitor the timeline and candidates for the permanent governorship appointment closely.

high.title: Business Groups Urge Perry Warjiyo's Successor to Stabilize the Rupiah
high.summary: Indonesian business association Apindo has responded to Bank Indonesia Governor Perry Warjiyo's resignation, urging a smooth leadership transition to maintain monetary policy continuity, institutional credibility, and market confidence. Businesses are particularly concerned about exchange rate volatility, global economic uncertainty, and high financing costs. The association stressed that the new governor must maintain clear, credible, and predictable policy communication to minimize market volatility and preserve investor trust.

high.title: Perry Warjiyo Resigns as Bank Indonesia Governor
high.summary: Bank Indonesia Governor Perry Warjiyo has officially resigned, with President Prabowo Subianto receiving his resignation letter on July 25, 2026. Senior Deputy Governor Destry Damayanti has been appointed as Acting Governor in the interim. This is a major market-moving event as leadership transitions at the central bank can significantly impact monetary policy direction and investor confidence in the Rupiah.

high.title: Destry Damayanti Appointed as Acting Bank Indonesia Governor
high.summary: Senior Deputy Governor Destry Damayanti has officially been named Acting Governor of Bank Indonesia following Perry Warjiyo's resignation submitted to President Prabowo Subianto. The appointment follows the mandate of the Bank Indonesia Law, ensuring continuity of central bank operations. Markets will closely watch whether monetary policy direction, including interest rate decisions, will remain stable under interim leadership.

high.title: Perry Warjiyo's Reason for Resigning as Bank Indonesia Governor
high.summary: Perry Warjiyo voluntarily resigned as Bank Indonesia Governor on July 25, 2026, citing personal reasons, with Destry Damayanti stepping in as Acting Governor. The voluntary nature of the resignation and the personal reasoning provided add uncertainty to the central bank's leadership outlook. Investors and market participants will be closely monitoring potential impacts on Indonesia's monetary policy and financial market stability.

high.title: Process for Selecting New Bank Indonesia Governor Following Perry Warjiyo's Resignation
high.summary: Following Perry Warjiyo's resignation, the process for appointing a new Bank Indonesia Governor is governed by Law No. 4 of 2026, an amendment to the P2SK law, which stipulates that the President will appoint a new governor to fill the vacancy. The selection process and timeline for a permanent replacement will be a key focus for financial markets, as the central bank's leadership directly influences monetary policy and Rupiah stability. Investors should monitor developments closely as prolonged uncertainty in BI leadership could affect market sentiment.

high.title: US Dollar Pressures Rupiah Again, Returns to Rp 18,000 Level
high.summary: The US dollar strengthened against the rupiah by 130.4 basis points (0.73%) to Rp 18,038, breaching the psychologically significant Rp 18,000 level. This depreciation is directly linked to the resignation of Bank Indonesia Governor Perry Warjiyo, which has triggered uncertainty in Indonesian financial markets. The rupiah's weakness signals growing investor concern over central bank leadership stability.

high.title: Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) Closes Lower Following Perry Warjiyo's Resignation as Bank Indonesia Governor
high.summary: The Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) closed down 10.64 points (0.17%) at 6,185.77, pressured by the announced resignation of Bank Indonesia Governor Perry Warjiyo. The index swung between a high of 6,219.41 and a low of 6,144.27 during the session, reflecting market uncertainty, with 341 stocks declining versus 307 advancing. Trading volume reached 27.75 billion shares with a turnover of Rp 12.15 trillion, indicating active repositioning by investors.

high.title: Rupiah Pressured by US Dollar After Perry Warjiyo Resigns as Bank Indonesia Governor
high.summary: The US dollar opened stronger against the rupiah at Rp 17,966 on Monday morning following the announcement of Perry Warjiyo's resignation as Bank Indonesia Governor, received by President Prabowo on Sunday (July 26). While the dollar weakened against other major currencies such as the Australian dollar, euro, Singapore dollar, and Chinese yuan, it gained ground specifically against the rupiah, highlighting Indonesia-specific risk. The leadership vacuum at Bank Indonesia raises concerns about monetary policy continuity and central bank independence.

medium.title: Gold Prices Stagnant Despite Renewed Middle East Tensions — Here's Why
medium.summary: Antam 24-karat gold prices rose only IDR 2,000 per gram during the July 20–25, 2026 trading period despite escalating Middle East tensions, a stark contrast to previous periods when gold surpassed IDR 3 million per gram. Analysts attribute the muted response to a shift in Indonesian investor behavior, with more funds being redirected into foreign currencies (forex) for short-term gains rather than gold as a safe-haven asset. This trend is important for investors tracking domestic commodity and currency markets.

medium.title: Africa's Economy Threatened by Super El Niño — Up to US$20 Billion in Losses Projected
medium.summary: The African Development Bank warns that Super El Niño could cut GDP of the most affected African nations by 1–2%, resulting in losses of US$10–20 billion across the continent, with farmers already losing nearly US$330 million due to drought this year. The fisheries sector is also expected to suffer from rising sea temperatures and storms. For Indonesian investors, this is a relevant global risk signal as El Niño also affects Indonesia's own agricultural output, commodity prices, and food inflation.

medium.title: Meat and Rice Prices Rise While Chili and Shallot Prices Drop
medium.summary: Indonesia's national strategic food price monitor (PIHPS) recorded mixed food commodity movements on July 5, 2026, with red cayenne pepper falling sharply by 7.93% to IDR 62,100/kg and shallots dropping 6% to IDR 47,800/kg, while meat and rice prices moved higher. The mixed price dynamics in key food commodities are relevant for monitoring inflation trends and household purchasing power in Indonesia.

medium.title: 200 Rural Banks (BPR/BPRS) Queue for Merger Approval — Here Are the Details
medium.summary: As of June 2026, 200 Rural Banks (BPR) and Islamic Rural Banks (BPRS) are in the process of obtaining merger or consolidation approval from the Financial Services Authority (OJK). Additionally, 81 BPR/BPRS have already been approved to consolidate into 24 entities, in line with OJK Regulation No. 7 of 2024. This large-scale consolidation wave reflects the government's push to strengthen the rural banking sector and improve financial stability.

medium.title: 9 Civil Servant Employees of National Nutrition Agency Facing Dismissal, 261 Non-Civil Servants Already Terminated
medium.summary: Indonesia's National Nutrition Agency (BGN) has dismissed 261 non-civil servant employees — comprising 224 non-ASN staff and 37 expert consultants — for misconduct, and is proceeding to terminate 9 civil servant employees. The dismissals reflect governance and compliance enforcement within a key government agency responsible for national nutrition programs. This may have implications for the operational capacity of BGN and public confidence in government nutrition initiatives.

medium.title: New Phenomenon: Groceries Now Increasingly Paid for with Buy Now Pay Later Services
medium.summary: A notable shift in consumer credit behavior is emerging in Indonesia, with Kredivo reporting that users are increasingly using Buy Now Pay Later (BNPL) services for everyday essentials like groceries and mobile credit top-ups, rather than high-ticket items like gadgets and electronics. This trend signals growing financial stress among Indonesian households and rising reliance on digital credit for basic needs. For investors, this shift highlights both an expanding BNPL market opportunity and potential credit risk concerns tied to consumer debt quality.

medium.title: BGN Chief Threatens to Fire SPPG Heads Who Mark Up Prices in Free Nutritious Meal Program
medium.summary: The head of Indonesia's National Nutrition Agency (BGN), Sudaryono, has issued a strong warning against price mark-ups by kitchen unit heads (SPPG) in the government's flagship Free Nutritious Meal (MBG) program, classifying such actions as corruption and gratification violations. Offenders face dismissal and kitchen suspension. This signals tighter governance and anti-corruption enforcement within the large-scale MBG program, which has significant government budget implications.

medium.title: BGN Chief Orders MBG Kitchen Units Not to Use Subsidized Gas, Cooking Oil, or Rice
medium.summary: BGN Chief Sudaryono has officially prohibited MBG program kitchen units (SPPG) from using government-subsidized goods, including Minyakita cooking oil, 3kg LPG cylinders, and SPHP subsidized rice. Violations will result in administrative sanctions and operational shutdowns. This policy is relevant to investors monitoring subsidy distribution efficiency and the integrity of Indonesia's large public nutrition spending program.

medium.title: BGN Develops Digital System for Parents to Monitor Free Nutritious Meal Program Menus
medium.summary: Indonesia's National Nutrition Agency (BGN) is developing a digital transparency platform that allows parents to track their children's school meal menus, cooking facilities, and nutritional content under the MBG program using their child's national ID number (NIK). The initiative reflects the government's push toward greater accountability and digital governance in its flagship nutrition program. This development is relevant to investors in the government digital services and food supply chain sectors linked to the MBG program.

medium.title: 9 Civil Servant Employees of National Nutrition Agency (BGN) Face Dismissal After 261 Non-Civil Servants Already Fired
medium.summary: The National Nutrition Agency (BGN) has dismissed 261 non-civil servant employees — including 224 staff and 37 expert personnel — for violations, with an additional 9 civil servants facing formal termination proceedings. The disciplinary action reflects governance and accountability measures within a key government agency overseeing Indonesia's national nutrition program. This may have implications for the operational capacity and budget execution of BGN, which is linked to broader government social spending programs.

medium.title: Pegadaian Records Net Profit of Rp 6.59 Trillion in H1 2026, Growing 84.4%
medium.summary: State-owned pawnbroker PT Pegadaian posted strong first-half 2026 results with net profit surging 84.4% year-on-year to Rp 6.59 trillion, driven by an adaptive business strategy and an expanding gold ecosystem. Total assets grew 53.9% to Rp 186.33 trillion, while gross outstanding loans rose 52.7% to Rp 155.1 trillion. Asset quality also improved, with the NPL ratio declining from 0.81% to 0.71%, making Pegadaian one of the standout performers among state-owned financial institutions.

medium.title: PT Pos Indonesia Finally Completes Rp 24 Billion Sukuk Yield Payment
medium.summary: PT Pos Indonesia (Persero) has completed its 6th periodic yield payment of Rp 24.118 billion for its Sukuk Ijarah Berkelanjutan I Series A-C (2024 issuance), processed through the Indonesian Central Securities Depository (KSEI) on July 24, 2026. The completion of this payment obligation is a positive signal for sukuk holders and bondholders monitoring the state-owned company's debt servicing capability. The word 'akhirnya' (finally) in the headline may suggest prior concerns about payment timeliness, worth monitoring for future obligations.
